title: Export reproducibility and deliverable evidence
prompt: A producer captured PNG frames on Linux and macOS using different installed fonts and GPUs. The report promises identical SHA-256 for every MP4 because both exports use 60 fps. One export has 299 decoded frames instead of 300, a narration starts late, and no decoded output samples were reviewed. Give a justified review and verification plan. Do not claim actual execution.

checks.reason: Routing-level signal only; assess reasoning and evidence through the rubric.

rubric: Rejects universal cross-machine hash guarantees and distinguishes scene-state, decoded-pixel and final-file identity.
Records scene and input hashes, seed, fonts, viewport/DPR, timebase, environment and capture/encoding parameters before comparing baselines.
Requires independent decoded frame count, timing, dimensions, sampled output frames and audio offset/end policy; does not hide a mismatch by unexplained trimming or retiming.
Separates technical export evidence from narrative quality and does not equate MP4/WebM or nominal fps with losslessness.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decisions, identifies discriminating project-level checks, and states evidence limits without inventing execution. Static validation and keyword matching do not prove runtime behavior.
